page.text:
The continuity of partial derivatives in the converse of the
Cauchy--Riemann theorem is essential. The mere existence of directional
derivatives along the coordinate axes satisfying $u_x = v_y$ and
$u_y = -v_x$ at an isolated point does not guarantee complex
differentiability. A classic counterexample is given by
$f(z) = \sqrt{|xy|}$ at the origin: both partial derivatives vanish at
$(0,0)$, trivially satisfying the Cauchy--Riemann equations, yet $f$
fails to be complex differentiable because the difference quotient along
diagonal directions $z = t(1+i)$ does not converge to $0$.

The deep *Looman--Menchoff Theorem* establishes the ultimate boundary of
this phenomenon: if $f$ is continuous on an open domain $U$ and its
partial derivatives $u_x, u_y, v_x, v_y$ exist everywhere on $U$ and
satisfy the Cauchy--Riemann equations almost everywhere, then $f$ is
holomorphic on $U$.
